cards.confidenceNote: Bilateral meetings, the airport greeting and the APEC speeches read on Kyiv Post and The Moscow Times; the three-way meeting had not been reported at run time.
cards.title: Trump meets Putin and Xi separately before Shenzhen three-way talks
cards.summary: Trump met Putin for nearly an hour and then Xi in Shenzhen on 19 November. The Kremlin said Ukraine was discussed and no important statements were made. Two Russian Tu-95 bombers landed in Vietnam two days earlier, and Xi and Putin criticised Western protectionism and sanctions at APEC.
cards.body:
The Shenzhen week opened with the parts that were certain to happen. Xi met Trump at the airport on 18 November, the first time he has done so for any visiting leader since becoming president, and on 19 November Trump held about an hour with Putin before sitting down with Xi. The Kremlin's readout, via aide Yuri Ushakov, was that the two discussed relations and Ukraine and that neither side made any particularly important statement. Trump told Xi the two countries should help end the war in Ukraine and said both want oil to move through Hormuz; Xi, in public, spoke only of stable ties.

Russia framed its arrival with force. Satellite images showed two Tu-95MS bombers, nuclear-capable with intercontinental range, at Da Nang in Vietnam on 17 November alongside two transports, the first such deployment there since the Soviet era. The same day Japan said two suspected Russian aircraft violated its airspace near Okinoshima, and South Korea and Taiwan tracked Russian aircraft in their air defence zones.

The three-way meeting was due on the afternoon of 19 November, Shenzhen time, after this card was written. Officials in all three capitals had set expectations low on arms control, and the Kremlin was the party talking about a joint statement. A meeting that ends with a photograph and no text would leave the greatpower reading where it is; an agreement to open strategic-stability talks would be the first arms-control step since New START lapsed in February.

Around the summit, the alignment underneath did not change. Before Trump arrived, Xi and Putin used their APEC speeches in Shenzhen to denounce Western trade protectionism and sanctions.

cards.confidenceNote: Charges and police statements read on BBC and The Guardian pages.
cards.title: US charges Russian with spying on Palantir staff in Silicon Valley
cards.summary: US prosecutors charged Russian national Igor D'iu with acting as a foreign agent to spy on staff of a defence firm that supplies Ukraine, which the BBC understands is Palantir. In Britain, police passed the case of a US Army officer suspected of spying for Russia to US authorities.
cards.body:
The case filed in northern California is a template of the hybrid campaign the board has tracked in Europe, now run on American soil. Prosecutors say Igor D'iu entered the US from Mexico in June after travelling from Istanbul, was recruited on Telegram, and was told by handlers who called Russia 'the Motherland' to gather information on a firm because its software was used against Russia in Ukraine. He allegedly photographed employees' laptop screens at a Palo Alto coffee shop and set up equipment his handlers could reach remotely. The US Attorney described a state-sponsored operation against a company 'because of that company's assistance to Ukraine.'

The second case moved jurisdiction rather than forward. Lt Col Brandon Tyner, arrested on 10 November at NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps headquarters in Gloucestershire on suspicion of offences under Britain's National Security Act, is now in US military custody; British counter-terrorism police said a decision was made to pass the investigation to US authorities. That makes a British charge in the case unlikely, and the question becomes whether the US Army brings one.

cards.confidenceNote: Strike and Gulf attacks read on BBC, NYT and Reuters text; damage on both sides unconfirmed.
cards.title: US strikes Qeshm missile site; Iran fires drones at Kuwait and Bahrain
cards.summary: US jets struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm late on 17 November. Iran then fired drones at Kuwait, its first attack there in two months, and at Bahrain. Two tankers were hit near Khasab on 16-17 November, with two seafarers missing and 11 injured.
cards.body:
The tactical picture changed from a blockade with occasional fire to an exchange. Iran's drones on Bahrain, four reported attacks in six days, were followed late on 17 November by US fighter jets striking a missile launch site on Qeshm Island with precision munitions, which US military officials described as a response to Iranian aggression against US personnel and assets. Iranian media reported explosions and no damage. Overnight Iran's army said it targeted US Patriot systems and launch platforms at Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait; Kuwait said it repelled the drones and reported no damage, and Bahrain reported more interceptions. Iran's armed forces chief warned of a stronger response 'without geographic limitations.'

At sea the cost rose. The LPG tanker Tara Gas, first hit seven nautical miles north of Khasab on 16 November, was struck again on 17 November and abandoned; Oman rescued 24 of 25 crew and an Indian seafarer is missing. An ADNOC L&S tanker was attacked the same evening, one crew member missing and 11 injured. Iran's Guard claimed fires on three ships; no one has named the attacker in the two casualty incidents.

The US widened the blockade rather than escorting through it: CENTCOM said ships taking cargo at sea from Iran-loaded vessels may be stopped, boarded, diverted or captured. The New York Times reports US and Israeli plans for renewed strikes most likely aimed at energy infrastructure, with no decision taken. That would be a step beyond the limited, defensive framing of the three US strike days since 2 November. Without a major-power-versus-major-power element, the kinetic reading stays in its band; the counting fact is that the Gulf states are again targets.

cards.confidenceNote: Trump remarks read via Iran International (Fox interview); Qatar statement via BBC and NYT.
cards.title: Trump calls the Islamabad deal 'a waste of time' as talks stall
cards.summary: Trump told Fox News the preliminary Islamabad understanding had been 'a waste of time' and said he would finish the war 'one way or the other.' Qatar, the mediator, called Iran's attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain a dangerous escalation. Trump said he would not ask Xi or Putin for help on Iran.
cards.body:
The diplomatic track is now a holding pattern with the US openly discounting it. Trump told Fox News that the preliminary understanding reached in Islamabad had been 'a waste of time,' useful only for assessing Tehran's approach, and that he wanted a lasting deal and would 'finish it off — soon. One way or the other.' He said he would not ask Xi or Putin for help because the US had defeated Iran's navy and air force and controlled the Strait. On 12 November he had told the Vice-President to drop the talks.

The mediators have not walked away. Qatar condemned Iran's attacks on its neighbours as a dangerous escalation that complicates efforts to contain tensions, and an Emirati official told the Manama Dialogue that the UAE does not believe a military solution is viable. The New York Times reports that Iran's leaders hardened their position after Trump's midterm losses, according to American, European and Iranian officials.

Two threat claims widen the gap. CNN reported, citing US officials, that Iran was preparing plans for a dirty bomb or chemical attack on senior US officials in Washington; the White House said there were no credible threats to the homeland, and Trump said Iran was 'looking at gas, looking at bio.' Neither claim has a government document behind it on the pages read.

What would move this card: a dated round of talks with both parties present, a Qatari or Omani text, or an Iranian offer that drops the two-day reopening conditions.

cards.confidenceNote: Gaza incursion read on NYT and France 24; joint strike planning is one NYT report citing officials.
cards.title: Israeli tanks cross Gaza ceasefire line as joint Iran strike plans reported
cards.summary: Israeli tanks crossed Gaza's ceasefire line on 18 November in the first armoured incursion since the truce, displacing 5,200 people. Israel killed Hamas's Rafah brigade commander on 14 November. US and Israeli officials have drawn up plans for renewed strikes on Iran, the New York Times reported.
cards.body:
Two Israeli moves in one week point the same way. On 18 November the military sent tanks and engineering machinery across the ceasefire line into Hamas-held central Gaza, calling it a limited raid on infrastructure that threatened its forces; the New York Times describes it as the first time heavy armour has gone far across that line since the truce. Hamas called it a blatant violation, and Gaza's civil defence said 5,200 people were displaced. Four days earlier a drone strike killed Rafah brigade commander Samir Abu Younis in al-Mawasi, which Hamas confirmed. Gaza's health ministry counts more than 1,600 people killed by Israeli fire during the ceasefire.

On Iran, the New York Times reports that American and Israeli military officials have drawn up plans for renewed strikes, most likely on energy infrastructure, with no decision taken. That is the relationship's operational core: planning together while the US President says he will finish the war one way or the other.

At home, Netanyahu remains caretaker while Gadi Eisenkot holds the mandate to form a government; Netanyahu keeps authority over the Gaza, Lebanon and Iran fronts in the meantime.

The tension to watch is Washington's own plan: the US-brokered Gaza framework rests on staged Israeli withdrawal, and an armoured raid outside the line tests whether Washington objects in public, as it did over Lebanon in August, or lets it pass.

cards.confidenceNote: Built from this run's read records; Shenzhen three-way outcome not yet known.
cards.title: US and Iran trade fire as Trump meets Putin and Xi in China
cards.summary: The US struck Qeshm and Iran fired at Kuwait and Bahrain while Trump met Putin and Xi in Shenzhen. Ukraine dropped part of the Crimean Bridge, Russia flew nuclear-capable bombers to Vietnam, and the IEA called Hormuz the largest energy-security threat in history. The risk index holds at 66.
cards.body:
Three arcs hit their week's peak at once, and none crossed into a new band. In the Gulf, the US strike on Qeshm, the first on Iranian territory in about ten days, was followed by Iran's drones on Kuwait and Bahrain; the board's kinetic reading already priced a war with strike days, so it holds at 75. The bar for 80, direct fighting between major powers, is not met.

In Europe, Ukraine's collapse of a Crimean Bridge road span is the war's most visible strike in months, and Russia's reply on Kyiv's bridges shows the infrastructure war going both ways. The alliance story is a public argument: a senior Pentagon official called deep strikes ineffective, and Germany and Britain rejected that in the same room. That is allies disagreeing while still coordinating, the 40-59 description, inside an axis that sits at 60 because of the halved Korea drills.

In Asia, Russia used bombers to remind its summit partners where it leads. The Shenzhen bilaterals happened; the three-way meeting is the question that could move the great-power or WMD readings, if it produces arms-control language.

For markets, the International Energy Agency's World Energy Outlook calls the Hormuz crisis the largest threat to energy security in history, and UK inflation rose to 3.6% on record fuel prices. EU gas storage stood at 69.95% on 17 November.

The combination to watch over the next week is a wider US strike campaign on Iran, which the New York Times says has been planned, landing while the summit's diplomacy is still being read.

cards.confidenceNote: Bridge collapse and Kyiv strikes read on BBC and Kyiv Independent; Trump-Putin readout on Kyiv Post.
cards.title: Ukraine brings down a Crimean Bridge span; Trump and Putin meet in Shenzhen
cards.summary: A Ukrainian missile and drone attack on 17 November dropped a road section of the Crimean Bridge into the Kerch Strait, and a third attack on 19 November halted rail traffic. Russian missiles damaged Kyiv's Dnipro bridges. Trump met Putin in Shenzhen; the Kremlin said no important statements were made.
cards.body:
Ukraine's strike on the Crimean Bridge is the war's sharpest blow to a Russian symbol since 2022. After a first attack overnight into 16 November, cruise missiles and drones on 17 November brought a large arched road section down into the water; Zelensky said it was a seven-stage operation weeks in the making, and the Kremlin promised to rebuild it 'even better than before.' A third attack early on 19 November halted rail services, Russia's transport ministry said. The bridge carries road and rail supply to Russian forces in the south.

Russia answered on Kyiv. Missiles damaged the Northern and Southern bridges over the Dnipro, closing both until traffic partly resumed and cutting water and heat, while attacks killed 14 people across Ukraine on 17 November and left 700,000 households without power in Dnipropetrovsk. Seven Russian drones entered Moldova the same day, and a Liberia-flagged LPG tanker sank in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone with no cause given.

The Western coalition argued in public. Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby told the Brussels contact group that deep strikes had not been effective in ending the war; Germany's defence minister called that 'quite a stupid thing' and Britain's defence secretary defended the strikes. Europe also reinforced its eastern edge: Poland sent riot police and a counter-terrorism unit to the Kaliningrad border after a reported Russian false-flag plot.

The channels: Trump met Putin for nearly an hour in Shenzhen on 19 November; the Kremlin said they discussed Ukraine and made no important statements. The prisoner exchange agreed in Abu Dhabi has not started. Europe was not in the room in Shenzhen.

iran_lead.title: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island; Iran fires drones at Kuwait and Bahrain
iran_lead.summary: US jets struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm late on 17 November, US military officials said. Iran answered with drones at Kuwait, its first attack there in two months, and Bahrain, its fourth in six days. Two tankers were hit near Khasab, leaving two seafarers missing and 11 injured.
facts: 17 November: US fighter jets struck a missile launch site on Qeshm Island with precision munitions, US military officials said; Iranian media reported explosions but no damage (BBC).
18 November: Kuwait said it repelled an Iranian drone attack, its first in more than two months; Iran's army said it targeted Patriot systems at Ali Al Salem air base (BBC).
18 November: Bahrain said it intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks, its fourth reported attack in six days (BBC; New York Times).
17 November: an ADNOC L&S tanker was attacked in Hormuz, one crew member missing and 11 injured; the Tara Gas was abandoned after a second hit (gCaptain, Reuters).
18 November: CENTCOM said ships receiving cargo at sea from Iran-loaded vessels may be stopped, boarded or captured (gCaptain, Reuters).
18 November: US and Israeli military officials have drawn up plans for renewed strikes most likely on energy infrastructure (New York Times).
17 November: the White House said there were no credible threats after CNN reported Iranian dirty-bomb planning (The Guardian).
iran_lead.changed: Iranian fire on the Gulf widened from Bahrain to Kuwait. After Iran's drones on Bahrain, the US hit Qeshm with precision munitions, and Iran's army said it targeted US Patriot systems at Kuwait's Ali Al Salem base. Qatar, the mediator, called Iran's attacks a dangerous escalation. CENTCOM extended the blockade to ship-to-ship transfers. The New York Times reports US and Israeli plans for renewed strikes on energy targets, and Trump called the Islamabad understanding a waste of time.
iran_lead.watch: Whether the US launches the wider strike campaign the New York Times describes; any death from Iranian fire in a Gulf state; who is firing at tankers north of Khasab; enforcement of the ship-to-ship rule; whether the Shenzhen meeting produces any Iran language; Iraq's 20 November deadline at Jurf al-Sakhar.

brics_lead.title: Trump meets Putin and Xi separately in Shenzhen before three-way talks
brics_lead.summary: Trump met Putin for nearly an hour and then Xi in Shenzhen on 19 November, before their first three-way meeting. Russia flew two nuclear-capable Tu-95 bombers to Vietnam, and Russian aircraft violated Japan's airspace on 17 November. The IAEA said North Korea finished the outside of a new Yongbyon enrichment hall.
brics_lead.changed: The bilateral meetings happened: the Kremlin said Ukraine was discussed but no important statements were made, and Trump told Xi both should help end the war and that both want oil to flow through Hormuz. Russia sent bombers to Vietnam, the first Russian bomber deployment there since the Soviet era, as Putin arrived. Allies moved too: Australia and the Philippines signed a defence pact, and Germany and Britain publicly rebutted a Pentagon official on Ukraine.
brics_lead.watch: What the three-way meeting produces, especially any nuclear-arms language; whether Trump meets Kim Jong Un; the Quad summit statement from Manila; any Chinese coast-guard surge after the summit; North Korean launches.

lenses.label: Bilateral US-China
lenses.oneline: Trump and Xi met in Shenzhen on 19 November; Trump said both want oil to flow through Hormuz.

lenses.label: BRICS bloc
lenses.oneline: No material bloc development in the window; Xi and Putin denounced Western trade protectionism and sanctions at APEC.

lenses.label: CRINK
lenses.oneline: Putin met Trump for nearly an hour; Russian nuclear-capable bombers landed in Vietnam; Yongbyon's new enrichment hall is externally complete.

lenses.label: Allies Cohesion
lenses.oneline: Australia and the Philippines signed a defence pact; Germany and Britain rejected US criticism of Ukraine's deep strikes.

facts: 19 November: Trump and Putin met for nearly an hour in Shenzhen; Kremlin aide Ushakov said neither side made particularly important statements (Kyiv Post).
19 November: Trump told Xi both should help end the war in Ukraine; Xi said he would work to keep ties stable (The Moscow Times).
17 November: two Russian Tu-95MS bombers landed at Da Nang, the first such deployment since the Soviet era (New York Times).
17 November: Japan said two suspected Russian aircraft violated its airspace near Okinoshima, a 'serious infringement' (BBC).
18 November: IAEA chief Grossi said the new Yongbyon extension had been externally complete since late October (France 24).
15 November: Australia and the Philippines signed a Defence Cooperation Arrangement (Defense News).

ukraine_lead.title: Ukraine brings down part of the Crimean Bridge as Russia hits Kyiv bridges
ukraine_lead.summary: A Ukrainian missile and drone attack on 17 November dropped a road section of the Crimean Bridge into the Kerch Strait; a third attack on 19 November halted rail traffic. Russian missiles damaged Kyiv's two Dnipro bridges, and attacks killed 14 people across Ukraine that day. Seven Russian drones entered Moldova.
facts: 17 November: a section of the Crimean Bridge collapsed into the water after a Ukrainian cruise-missile and drone attack; the Kremlin said it would rebuild (BBC).
19 November: Crimea's Moscow-installed head said traffic was suspended after a third attack; rail services were halted (BBC).
17 November: Russian attacks damaged Kyiv's Northern and Southern bridges and killed 14 people across Ukraine; the Air Force counted 306 attack drones plus missiles (Kyiv Independent).
17 November: Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby said deep strikes had not been effective; Germany's Pistorius and Britain's Streeting rejected that (Kyiv Independent, Reuters).
17 November: seven Russian drones entered Moldova's airspace; Moldova summoned Russia's envoy on 18 November (Politico).
17 November: the LPG tanker Gas Husky sank in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone, cause not given (gCaptain, Reuters).
18 November: Rzeczpospolita reported a Russian false-flag plot near Kaliningrad; Poland sent about 180 riot police to the border (Kyiv Independent).
ukraine_lead.changed: Ukraine brought down a road section of the bridge, its heaviest damage since the 2022 blast; Zelensky called it a seven-stage operation, and the Kremlin says it will rebuild. Russia answered on Kyiv's bridges and energy grid. A senior Pentagon official called deep strikes ineffective at the Brussels contact group, and Germany and Britain rejected that. Moldova summoned Russia's envoy over drones, and Poland reinforced its Kaliningrad border after a reported false-flag plot.
ukraine_lead.watch: Whether rail traffic resumes across the Kerch Strait; Russia's answer to the bridge strike; what Trump and Putin agreed on Ukraine in Shenzhen; the start of the agreed prisoner exchange; Estonia's crossings closing on 1 December; further ship sinkings off Bulgaria.
